budget_items.what_was_said: Of 37 abatement applications, 22 were granted and 15 denied, with four additional administrative abatements for solar, fire and land corrections. The principal assessor gave a total dollar amount of abatements granted.

budget_items.topic: State reimbursement forms (veterans exemption, motor vehicle excise)
budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor submitted the MDM1 veterans exemption and motor vehicle excise reimbursement forms for FY2025, describing separate reimbursement amounts that together came to nearly the stated total from the state.
The board received a vendor credit but costs for postcards and postage were said to exceed it, with an invoice for the postcards questioned for lacking supporting data before being signed.
A property owner who wants to stay in chapter land must pay a fee to record a lien at the registry of deeds, which the office offered to handle as a courtesy.

budget_items.topic: Neighborhood site index / special project funding
budget_items.what_was_said: Town meeting approved a special project article (not a capital request) funding a first installment of work to review and correct neighborhood site index assignments.

budget_items.topic: Means-tested senior exemption levy cap and payout scenarios
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed using a percentage of the tax levy to cap the means-tested senior exemption program and modeled how many applicants could be supported at full versus partial payout.

decisions.decision: Cyclical inspections will begin the week of May 12, with streets to be inspected posted as they are identified.
The assessors' office will go to the registry of deeds as a courtesy to record chapter land liens once a property owner pays the fee.
Going forward, incomplete applications will be stamped as received with the date and marked incomplete rather than processed as complete submissions.
Linda McQuade will draft revised denial-notice language identifying reasons for denial and send it to the board before the next meeting.
The principal assessor will compile the total cost overrun on the cyclical inspection contract and go back to the vendor about it.
The 'How to Read Your Vision Card' document will be kept generic/timeless, with year-specific data moved to a separate report.
The office will request a data report from Vision for commercial properties similar to the residential/condo report received.
The next meeting will move from May 21 to May 19 to accommodate a scheduling conflict.
The board will meet once a month over the summer (June, July, August) as it did the prior year.
The board will aim to hold the classification hearing in late October so the tax rate can be set by November 1.

votes.motion: Accept the minutes of February 19th as amended.
Adjourn open session and enter executive session under purpose 7, regarding abatement/exemption applications.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting passed updated income and asset limits for the senior tax exemption/deferral program (clauses 41 and 17); the board's formal review is still pending.
The board began modeling a levy-cap-based means-tested senior exemption, weighing full versus partial payouts, but deferred a decision to bring back figures.
Cyclical property inspections start the week of May 12, with streets posted as they are identified.
The board directed that incomplete abatement/exemption applications be stamped received and marked incomplete rather than treated as complete, and asked for denial notices to state reasons.
This was board member John Rabbit's final meeting.

why_it_matters: A senior resident's exemption or deferral eligibility and payout could change once the board finishes reviewing the new Town Meeting-approved limits and any levy-based cap.
Cyclical inspections beginning May 12 mean some property owners will see an assessor at their door or a mailed notice tied to their assessed value.
Applicants for abatements or exemptions will now get a dated 'incomplete' stamp and, once drafted, a notice stating the specific reason for any denial.
watch_next: Next Board of Assessors meeting (moved to May 19) for the levy-cap exemption payout figures

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely wherever both touch the same concrete item — the May 12 inspection restart, the $500 vendor credit, the $190 postcard invoice, the $103k/$12,142 reimbursement figures, and the May 19/21 date swap — but they cover largely different territory otherwise: ours has no record at all of the executive session (abatement denial, the $5,054.85 DOR-approved abatement, Chapter 61A liens) or of several open-session items (the taxpayer complaint letter, the DOR Neighborhood/Site Index item, minutes approvals), while the official minutes have none of the extended means-tested senior exemption/levy-cap figures or several process decisions (the lien-fee courtesy trip to the registry, incomplete-application stamping, denial-notice language, the summer meeting cadence) that our minutes describe in detail. A reader should specifically check the "27,000" abatement total (official ties $27,106.21 to "2026" while ours labels it "FY2025"), the "300" postcard figure against official's "220," and whether an August summer meeting was actually set, since official's upcoming-meetings list only shows June 11 and July 16.
